newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Garibaldi company dropped from manslaughter charges.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Garibaldi company dropped from manslaughter charges.

text.p: A manslaughter charge against the collapsed smallgoods company, Garibaldi Smallgoods Pty Ltd, has been dropped, the South Australian Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) Paul Rofe said on Monday.

Rofe told Reuters manslaughter charges remained against three former Garibaldi executives Lou Marchi, Philip Marchi and Neville Mead, following the death of a four-year old girl in 1995 from complications after eating Garibaldi garlic mettwurst.

Rofe said the decision to drop the charge against the company, now in liquidation, was made on pragmatic financial grounds, given the company did not qualify for legal aid and would have to be legally represented at the state's expense.
"In the event of a conviction, all we could do was fine them and they have not got any money," he said.

A coronial inquiry found that Nikki Robinson, 4, died after contracting haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS) as a result of eating garlic mettwurst, while another 150 people were affected by the HUS outbreak.
A trial date for the charges against the three former managers had been set for late February 1997, Rofe said.
